steps.description: Verify that the patient's insurance policy is active and covers MRI diagnostics. Open the HIS Insurance Module, search by policy number, and confirm coverage status shows 'Active' and MRI is listed under covered procedures.

Obtain the exact procedure code and diagnosis code from the referring physician's order. The procedure code must match the TPA's approved code list; confirm the diagnosis code is ICD-10 formatted. Document the scheduled MRI date and the referring physician's ID.

Submit the pre-authorization request through the insurer's TPA portal using all collected details. Attach the physician's referral note and any prior investigation reports. Note the portal submission reference number in the HIS.

Monitor the TPA portal for authorization status. Approval is expected within 2–4 hours. If rejected, immediately notify the TPA Escalation Manager and counsel the patient on out-of-pocket payment options before proceeding.

Once authorization is received, update the HIS record with the authorization number and notify the Radiology scheduling desk to confirm the MRI slot. File the written authorization in the patient's physical and electronic record.

Confirm the treating physician has entered the discharge order in HIS and the discharge summary is complete (diagnoses coded, medications listed, follow-up instructions included). Flag incomplete summaries to the Medical Superintendent within 24 hours.

Generate the final itemized bill through the HIS Billing Module. Verify all charges are accurate, apply any approved waivers or insurance adjustments, and present the final bill to the patient or guardian for review.

If the patient is insured, submit the discharge claim package to the TPA desk for processing. The TPA desk must confirm claim submission before the patient is cleared for discharge unless payment is settled out-of-pocket.
Collect payment (cash, card, or insurance clearance letter). Issue the official receipt from the HIS Cashier Module. Ensure zero balance before proceeding.

Prepare the discharge package for the patient: printed discharge summary, medication list, follow-up appointment card, and diet/activity instructions. Provide digital copies via the patient portal if registered.

Update the patient's bed status to 'Discharged' in the HIS Bed Management Module. Notify housekeeping to prepare the bed for the next patient. Archive the patient record and close the encounter in HIS.

The billing staff must identify the incorrect charge and document the original charge code, the erroneous amount, and the correct amount. Collect supporting documentation such as the service order, physician note, or pharmacy dispensing record that justifies the correction.

Raise a Billing Correction Request in the HIS Billing Module, attaching all supporting documents. The request will be automatically routed to the Billing Supervisor for amounts between $500 and $1,999, or to the Finance Controller for amounts $2,000 and above.

Billing Supervisor reviews the request within 4 business hours. If approved, the correction is applied in HIS. If rejected, the reason is documented and communicated to the requesting staff. Amounts over $2,000 require Finance Controller countersignature.

Once approved, apply the corrected charge in HIS and generate a revised bill for the patient. Notify the patient of the correction and issue a written explanation. Update the audit trail entry with the approver's employee ID.

Verify the physician's bed request form in HIS, confirming the required bed type (General, Semi-Private, Private, ICU, ICCU, NICU, HDU) and clinical priority. Cross-check the patient's insurance coverage or payment category to confirm eligibility for the requested bed class.

Check real-time bed availability in the HIS Bed Management Module for the requested type. If the requested type is unavailable, offer the next available class or add the patient to the waitlist. Notify the patient or family of the wait time.

Assign the bed in HIS, print the bed assignment slip, and escort or direct the patient to the ward. Update the bed status to 'Occupied' in HIS within 15 minutes of the patient reaching the ward. Notify the receiving ward nurse of the incoming patient.

Receive the patient's request either in person at the Medical Records counter or via the HIS Patient Portal. Verify the patient's identity using two forms of ID (government photo ID + hospital ID or appointment card). Check that Form MR-REQ-01 is fully completed.

If the request is from an authorized representative (not the patient), verify the notarized authorization letter or legal power of attorney. For subpoenas or court orders, immediately escalate to the Legal & Compliance department before proceeding.

Retrieve the requested records from the HIS Archive. For urgent requests (24-hour turnaround), ensure HOD approval is documented in the system. Verify all requested documents are present and complete before packaging.
Prepare physical copies (printed, collated, sealed) or provide digital access via the patient portal. Collect the document processing fee as per the hospital's fee schedule before releasing records.

Log the release in the Medical Records Disclosure Register: requestor name, ID, relationship to patient, purpose, date, documents provided, and processing staff's ID. Retain a copy of the patient's authorization form with the register entry.

Department HOD submits Form IT-ACC-01 via the HIS IT Request Module at least 48 hours before the new staff member's start date. The form must include: employee ID, role, department, required systems, and start date.

IT Administration verifies the request against the RBAC access matrix for the employee's role. Confirm access levels are appropriate — no over-provisioning. If the role requires elevated privileges, IT Manager approval is required before proceeding.

Provision HIS login credentials, hospital email account, and role-specific module access within 24 hours. Generate a temporary password and communicate it securely to the employee via their personal email or department HOD.

Confirm the employee has logged in and changed their temporary password within 48 hours. Log the provisioning event in the IT Audit System with timestamps. Notify IT Manager if password change is not completed within the deadline.

Compile the complete claim package within 24 hours of patient discharge: discharge summary (physician-signed), itemized bill, all investigation reports, pre-authorization approval letter, and signed consent forms. Use the insurer-specific claim form from the HIS Forms Library.

Upload the complete claim package to the insurer's TPA portal and record the portal submission reference number in the HIS. Simultaneously send a physical copy by courier; retain the courier tracking number.

Track claim status on the TPA portal daily. Respond to any queries from the TPA within 24 hours. Escalate to the TPA Escalation Manager if the claim is pending for more than 5 business days without resolution.

On receiving the settlement or rejection notice, update the HIS record. For partial approvals or rejections, notify the Billing Department within 2 hours and coordinate patient counselling on outstanding balances. Close the claim record in HIS.

Report the equipment failure immediately via the HIS Asset Management Module or call the Biomedical Help Desk (ext. 4400). Provide: equipment ID, physical location (ward and room number), nature of the fault, time of failure, and whether a patient was affected at the time.

Biomedical Engineering acknowledges within 15 minutes and dispatches a technician. The reporting department must arrange a substitute device from the central equipment store while the primary device is under repair. Document the substitute device ID in the downtime log.

Once the device is repaired or replaced, the Biomedical technician closes the work order in HIS with the repair details, parts replaced, and test results confirming the device is safe for use. The ward head must sign off on the return-to-service form before the device is put back into clinical use.

Confirm the stock-out by checking the HIS Pharmacy Module inventory for the drug name, current stock level, and last dispensed date. Verify that no other pharmacy store in the hospital holds available stock. Document the drug name, strength, and quantity required in the Pharmacy Incident Register.

Immediately notify the treating physician and the ward nursing station of the stock-out. Provide a realistic estimated resupply timeline. Simultaneously raise an emergency procurement request in the HIS Pharmacy Module and contact at least two approved alternative suppliers from the approved vendor list.

If the drug cannot be sourced from any vendor within 4 hours, escalate to the Pharmacy Head and simultaneously notify the Medical Superintendent to determine if a therapeutic substitution is clinically appropriate. The physician must document the substitution decision in the patient's HIS record.

Once the drug is procured and received, verify quantity, expiry date, and batch number against the purchase order. Update the HIS Pharmacy inventory, close the incident in the Pharmacy Incident Register, and submit a root-cause analysis to Pharmacy Management within 48 hours.

Identify the reason for specimen rejection: mislabelling, hemolysis, clot in anticoagulated tube, incorrect container, inadequate volume, temperature deviation, or exceeded transport time. Log the rejection reason in the Laboratory Information System (LIS) with timestamp and specimen ID.

Notify the requesting department (ward or OPD) within 30 minutes of rejection. Provide specific instructions on correct specimen type, container colour, labelling format, volume required, and transport time limit for re-collection. Update the order status in HIS to 'Specimen Rejected — Re-collection Required'.

The ward nursing staff or phlebotomist must re-collect the specimen following the corrected procedure. A new label must be generated from HIS; previously printed labels must not be reused. For time-sensitive tests (blood gas, cultures), re-collection must happen within 30 minutes of notification.

Process the re-collected specimen and update the order status in LIS. Communicate revised TAT to the requesting team. If the same patient has repeated specimen rejections (2 or more in one admission), escalate to the Laboratory Supervisor and report as a quality event in the HIS Quality Module.

workflow_name: Patient Safety Incident Reporting and Review

steps.description: The staff member who witnessed or discovered the incident must complete the Incident Report Form (Form QA-INC-01) in the HIS Quality Module within 2 hours of the event. Include: date, time, location, persons involved, nature of the incident, immediate actions taken, and patient outcome. Do not delay reporting to investigate first.

Department Supervisor reviews the incident report and adds their assessment within 4 hours. For sentinel events (unexpected death or serious injury), the Supervisor must immediately notify the Quality & Patient Safety Officer and Medical Superintendent verbally — do not wait for the written report.

Quality & Patient Safety Officer assesses the incident for severity level (Minor, Moderate, Major, Sentinel) and determines if a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is required. Major and Sentinel events always require RCA; Minor and Moderate events require at least a concise review with documented findings.

For RCA-required events, convene the RCA team (department head, relevant clinical lead, Quality Officer) within 72 hours. Document contributing factors, root causes, and corrective action plan with assigned owners and target dates in the HIS Quality Module.

Present the RCA findings and corrective actions at the monthly Quality Committee meeting. Monitor implementation of corrective actions via the HIS Quality Module tracking dashboard. Submit aggregated incident data to the Medical Director quarterly for trending and systemic improvements.

Identify the correct consent form for the planned procedure from the HIS Forms Library (e.g., FORM-CONSENT-SUR-01 for surgical procedures, FORM-CONSENT-BT-01 for blood transfusions). Confirm the correct form version is current; outdated versions must not be used.

The treating physician or designated clinical staff must explain the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives to the patient in their preferred language. If the patient requires an interpreter, arrange one before proceeding. Do not obtain consent in a language the patient does not understand.

The patient (or legal representative for incapacitated patients) signs the consent form in the presence of the physician and a nurse witness. Both the physician and witness must sign with their staff IDs. For emergency situations where signed consent cannot be obtained, document the clinical justification and two-witness verbal consent.

Scan the signed consent form and upload it to the patient's HIS record immediately. The procedure must not commence until the consent document is confirmed in the system. The paper original must be filed in the patient's physical medical record folder.

Retrieve the PM work order auto-generated by the HIS Asset Management Module 30 days before the due date. Confirm the equipment ID, location, last PM date, and the PM checklist specific to the equipment type. Coordinate with the ward or department for a scheduled downtime window to perform the maintenance without disrupting patient care.

Perform the preventive maintenance tasks as specified in the equipment's PM checklist: clean components, replace consumables (filters, batteries, sensors), lubricate moving parts, tighten electrical connections, and test all alarm and safety systems. Record all findings and readings in the PM work order.

Run functional performance tests to confirm the equipment meets the manufacturer's performance specifications post-maintenance. If calibration is due, perform calibration using traceable standards and upload the calibration certificate to the HIS equipment file.

Close the PM work order in HIS with: technician's employee ID, PM completion date, test results, parts replaced, and next PM due date. The equipment's PM compliance status must update to 'Compliant' in the system. Print and attach the PM completion sticker to the equipment. Notify the ward head that the equipment is returned to service.

Upon detecting HIS downtime, the IT Helpdesk must immediately broadcast an alert to all department heads via the hospital PA system, group messaging, and the IT incident management system. Clearly state: the time of onset, affected systems, and estimated resolution time if known.

All clinical and operational departments must activate downtime procedures: retrieve physical downtime folders from each nursing station and department desk. Begin recording all registrations, orders, medication administrations, lab results, and billing on the pre-printed paper forms.

IT must work to restore system access, providing status updates every 60 minutes until resolution. Activate failover or backup systems if available. Escalate to IT Manager within 30 minutes of onset for unplanned outages; planned maintenance must have pre-approval 48 hours in advance.

Once HIS is restored, all downtime records must be entered into HIS within 2 hours by the responsible department staff. IT must verify data integrity for all critical systems (medication orders, lab results, billing transactions) before issuing the 'System Restored' notification. Conduct a post-incident review within 48 hours.

The attending physician enters the transfer order in the HIS Clinical Module, specifying: the clinical reason for transfer, destination ward, patient's current condition, and any isolation or monitoring requirements. Transfer orders must not be executed based on verbal instructions alone.

The Case Manager confirms bed availability in the destination ward via the HIS Bed Management Module. Contact the receiving ward charge nurse to confirm readiness for the patient. If ICU transfer is involved, ensure attending physician sign-off is documented in HIS before proceeding.

The transferring nurse conducts a formal clinical handover to the receiving nurse using the SBAR framework: Situation (why transferring), Background (diagnosis, history), Assessment (current status), Recommendation (care plan). Document the handover in the patient's HIS Nursing Notes.

Transfer the patient physically with all essential items: medications, IV infusions, patient belongings, and physical medical record folder. Upon arrival at the destination ward, update the patient's bed status and location in the HIS Bed Management Module within 15 minutes.
